text: So much of what we were doing was influenced by gut, by trying to connect with people, listening to them.
speaker: Claire Butler
context: Lenny asks Claire to explain what a bottom-up go-to-market motion is and how it applies to Figma. Claire clarifies that this approach emphasizes individual contributors (ICs) who spend significant time using the product. She reflects on how their strategy has evolved, mentioning that their focus has shifted from gut feelings to creating a repeatable process that resonates with users, particularly designers, who are central to their market.
text_ko: 우리가 하던 일의 많은 부분이 직감에 의존했어요—사람들과 연결하려고 노력하고 그들의 이야기를 들으면서 결정한 경우가 많았거든요.
text_zh: 我们当时做的很多事情都是凭感觉，想办法和大家建立联系，多听听他们怎么说。
text_es: Gran parte de lo que hacíamos salía del instinto, de tratar de conectar con la gente, de escucharlos de verdad.
key_sentence: by trying to connect with people, listening to them.
original_text: So much of what we were doing was influenced by gut, by trying to connect with people, listening to them. But when I look back is when I'm like, 'Oh, this is a repeatable motion.' So when I look back at it, I would say that if I were to define and think about how I define our go-to-market motion, and we've said it, we've called it a lot of things over time. We called it product-led, we called it community-led. The way I think about it now is this bottoms-up motion, that really is focused on ICs.

vocabulary.definition: To have an effect on the character, development, or behavior of someone or something.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being influenced often refers to how decisions, strategies, or company culture are shaped by external factors such as market trends, customer feedback, or leadership styles.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'influenced' suggests a degree of persuasion or impact, it can imply both positive and negative effects depending on the context.

vocabulary.definition: To join or establish a relationship or link between people or ideas.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business setting, to connect often refers to networking, building relationships with clients, or fostering collaboration among team members.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'connect' carries a positive connotation, suggesting engagement and relationship-building rather than mere association.

vocabulary.definition: The active process of receiving and interpreting spoken messages.
vocabulary.businessContext: Effective listening is crucial in business for understanding client needs, facilitating team communication, and gathering feedback for improvement.
vocabulary.nuance: Listening implies more than just hearing; it suggests an active effort to understand and respond appropriately to what is being communicated.

text: One of the things that I did was really try to not market. And that's so funny as a marketer to say that, but that was really core to build authenticity with people.
speaker: Claire Butler
context: Claire discusses her approach to building credibility for Figma in the early days, highlighting that designers are often skeptical of marketing. She emphasizes the importance of authenticity and how she focused on showcasing the technical features of the product rather than traditional marketing tactics. By collaborating closely with the design and engineering teams, Figma aimed to create genuine connections with early users, which helped build trust.
text_ko: 제가 한 일 중 하나는 일부러 마케팅을 하지 않으려고 정말 노력한 거예요. 마케터로서 이런 말을 한다는 게 웃기긴 한데, 그게 사람들에게 진정성을 보여주는 데 핵심이었어요.
text_zh: 我当时做的一件事就是尽量不去做营销。听起来很搞笑对吧，我一个做营销的人这么说，但这确实是和用户建立真实关系的核心。
text_es: Una de las cosas que hice fue tratar de no hacer marketing como tal. Y suena súper raro que lo diga siendo marketer, pero eso fue clave para generar confianza genuina con la gente.
key_sentence: Core to build authenticity was not marketing.
original_text: One of the things that I did was really try to not market. And that's so funny as a marketer to say that, but that was really core to build authenticity with people. And so the way that we did that in the early days was what we had was the tool, and that's pretty much what we had, and we had a design team and we had an engineering team.

vocabulary.definition: The quality of being genuine, real, and true to one's values or beliefs.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, authenticity is crucial for building trust with customers and stakeholders, as it reflects a company's commitment to transparency and integrity.
vocabulary.nuance: While authenticity is often seen as a positive trait, it can also imply a lack of polish or professionalism if not balanced appropriately.

vocabulary.definition: The central or most important part of something, often serving as the foundation for further development.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a business context, identifying the core values or competencies of a company is essential for strategic planning and decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'core' often refers to fundamental aspects, it can also imply a focus on simplicity and clarity in complex environments.

text: So, we have a couple tiers. We have a free tier and then we have a pro tier, and then we have our org tier. And the free tier, free tier includes this free starter team.
speaker: Claire Butler
context: Lenny inquires about Figma's pricing structure and how it impacts user adoption. Claire explains the different tiers of Figma's service, highlighting the importance of the free tier as an entry point for users. She mentions that the free tier allows for a starter team without immediate payment, which encourages users to explore the product and build confidence before committing to the paid tiers.
text_ko: 그래서 저희는 티어가 세 가지 있어요: 무료 티어(free tier), 프로 티어(pro tier), 그리고 조직용 티어(org tier). 무료 티어에는 무료 스타터 팀(free starter team)이 포함돼요.
text_zh: 我们分几个档次，有免费版，还有专业版(pro tier)，然后是企业版(org tier)。免费版里面包含了一个免费的入门团队套餐。
text_es: Entonces, tenemos varios niveles. Tenemos el nivel gratuito, después el nivel pro, y luego está nuestro nivel para organizaciones. Y el nivel gratuito incluye este equipo inicial sin costo.
key_sentence: So, we have a couple tiers.
original_text: So, we have a couple tiers. We have a free tier and then we have a pro tier, and then we have our org tier. And the free tier, free tier includes this free starter team. And so you can just do that, go to figma.com, and go do that. Pro is all enter credit card, and then org is you talk to sales.

vocabulary.definition: A tier refers to a level or rank within a structured system, often indicating different categories or classes of products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and technology, tiers are commonly used to categorize service offerings, such as subscription plans that provide varying levels of features and support.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'tier' often implies a hierarchy, suggesting that higher tiers offer more value or benefits compared to lower ones.

text: I think that one of the ... I don't know about requirements, but things that makes this a lot more likely to be successful, is that your IC, there's a tool, and they can use it on their own. And it's technical.
speaker: Claire Butler
context: Claire reflects on the prerequisites for successfully implementing a bottoms-up go-to-market strategy. She emphasizes that a technical product that individual contributors (ICs) can use independently increases the likelihood of success. This autonomy allows users to build confidence in the product, which is crucial for fostering adoption within organizations.
text_ko: 요구사항은 잘 모르겠지만, 성공 가능성을 훨씬 높이는 요인 중 하나는 개인 기여자(IC)가 그 도구(tool)를 혼자서도 쓸 수 있다는 점이에요. 그리고 그 도구가 기술적이에요.
text_zh: 我觉得这个项目成功的关键因素之一，虽然不能说是硬性要求吧，但就是你的一线员工(IC)得有个工具，而且他们能自己上手操作。这个工具还得是技术性的。
text_es: Yo creo que una de las... no sé si llamarlas requisitos, pero una de las cosas que hace que esto tenga muchas más probabilidades de éxito, es que tu colaborador individual (IC) tenga una herramienta que pueda usar por su cuenta. Y que sea técnica.
key_sentence: things that makes this a lot more likely to be successful, is that your IC, there's a tool, and they can use it on their own.
original_text: I think that one of the ... I don't know about requirements, but things that makes this a lot more likely to be successful, is that your IC, there's a tool, and they can use it on their own. And it's technical. I think that helps a ton.

vocabulary.definition: Technical relates to the practical aspects of a particular field, often involving specialized knowledge or skills.
vocabulary.businessContext: In technology and business, 'technical' often describes tools, processes, or knowledge that require expertise, such as software development or engineering.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply complexity and is often used to differentiate between general and specialized knowledge or tasks.

text: I think the key thing is that you have to keep doing it.
speaker: Claire Butler
context: Claire discusses how Figma's growth necessitates a balance between maintaining the successful bottoms-up approach while integrating more traditional top-down strategies. She highlights the importance of continuous advocacy for the core values and methodologies that initially drove Figma's success, even as the company scales and faces new challenges.
text_ko: 제 생각엔 핵심은 꾸준히 해나가야 한다는 점이에요.
text_zh: 关键是你得坚持做下去。
text_es: La clave está en no parar, hay que seguir haciéndolo.
key_sentence: you have to keep doing it.
original_text: I think the key thing is that you have to keep doing it. One of the things that I feel like, at my role now at Figma, that I think a lot about, is how I can keep advocating for this stuff when we are starting to implement more top down motion, and having to really prove ROI.

text: I remember there was a specific instance, I think it was last year, maybe two years ago, where there was this issue with these servers and an AWS cluster went down and we didn't know what was going on.
speaker: Claire Butler
context: Claire recounts a challenging experience at Figma involving server downtime and the subsequent backlash from users. She emphasizes the importance of transparency during crises and how the team chose to publicly address the issues. By openly communicating with users, Figma aimed to maintain trust and demonstrate accountability, which is essential for sustaining user relationships.
text_ko: 특정한 경우가 하나 생각나요. 아마 작년, 혹은 2년 전쯤에 이 서버들(servers)에 문제가 생겨 AWS 클러스터(AWS cluster)가 다운됐는데 무슨 일이 벌어지고 있는지 전혀 모르고 있었어요.
text_zh: 我记得有一次，好像是去年还是前年吧，服务器出了问题，AWS的一个集群挂了，我们当时完全搞不清楚怎么回事。
text_es: Recuerdo que hubo una vez, creo que fue el año pasado o hace dos años, cuando tuvimos un problema con unos servidores y se nos cayó un clúster de AWS y no teníamos ni idea de qué estaba pasando.
key_sentence: an AWS cluster went down and we didn't know what was going on.
original_text: I remember there was a specific instance, I think it was last year, maybe two years ago, where there was this issue with these servers and an AWS cluster went down and we didn't know what was going on. And so we had downtime multiple times in a week and people were pissed, right? Things were not going well.

vocabulary.definition: A specific occurrence or example of something, often used to illustrate a point or provide context.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business discussions, citing an instance can help clarify a situation, support an argument, or demonstrate the implications of a particular decision or event.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'instance' is often neutral, it can imply that the example is one of many, and should be used when specificity is needed without suggesting that it is the only case.
